newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's main union body extends strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's main union body extends strike.

text.p: South Korea's biggest union organisation called on its 1.2 million members to extend a 24-hour strike planned to begin on Friday until the end of this year, the union leader said.
Park In-sang, chairman of the Federation of Korean Trade Unions, told a news conference a decision on whether to further extend the stoppage would be taken on December 30.
"We have decided to strike from 1.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) on December 27 until the end of the year," Park said. "We will fight for democracy and the livelihood of the workers."
Park said bus services in six major cities, including Seoul, would be halted.

Gas, electricity and phone services would not be affected unless the strikes continue "and are carried out to extremes", Park said, adding that efforts would be made not to disrupt life for ordinary South Korean citizens.

The federation is the only union umbrella group recognised by the government. Its outlawed counterpart, the Korea Confederation of Trade Unions, called out its 500,000 members on an indefinite strike on Thursday.
